title: The Hungry Visitor
premise: Theo Zhou returns to the condemned Holloway house for a routine appraisal and finds his childhood imaginary friend, Wren, waiting on the porch—unchanged after thirty years, still humming the song they invented together. The house feeds on unfinished grief, and Wren is its lure: the last verse of their song was never written because Theo abandoned it the night his sister drowned. As frost creeps across the windows spelling out names, Theo must recover what really happened that night, choose between protecting his mother's lie and honoring his sister's truth, and learn the final verse without singing along—because those who sing it become part of the house's chorus. In the end, Theo sings only the melody while speaking the words aloud, freeing his sister's voice from the walls and letting the house starve; he walks out at dawn as the appraisal comes back: zero.
about_author: Ada Dunmore is the pen name of a former rural property assessor who spent a decade cataloguing houses no one would buy. She writes horror about buildings that remember, drawing on her habit of talking to empty rooms to keep them honest.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Theo. He arrives at the Holloway house with a clipboard and professional detachment, noting sagging porches and a buyer eager to flip it. The rooms measure wrong—hallways longer inside than out. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Porch Light
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At dusk, a small figure sits on the porch steps: Wren, his imaginary friend, exactly as left at age nine. Wren greets him by name and hums the first two verses of their old song. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition—the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He inventories the house to steady himself: eleven doors, then twelve, then thirteen. Each extra door opens onto his childhood bedroom. Wren appears in doorframes, patient, humming. Emotional beat: the rational mind building scaffolding over panic.

chapters.title: The Song Without an End
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Theo's POV. 1994: Theo and Wren sing through the house while his sister Mei plays downstairs. They always stop before the last verse—Wren says the ending isn't theirs yet. Emotional beat: golden nostalgia curdling with dramatic irony.

chapters.title: What the Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Present day, phone call scene, Theo's POV. His mother begs him to leave the house, her voice cracking in ways thirty years of silence never allowed. She mentions Mei unprompted for the first time since the funeral. Emotional beat: loyalty straining against a buried truth.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, overnight in the house. Frost blooms across every window in ferning patterns that resolve into letters: names, dozens, including MEI. Wren watches from the hallway, humming. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose—the house is keeping records.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The flipper's agent arrives, walks through smiling, and leaves without a shadow or footprints. Theo checks his own paperwork: his name is already signed on documents he never touched. Emotional beat: realization that leaving was never on offer.

chapters.title: Second Verse, Same as the First
chapters.summary: Alternating present and memory, Theo's POV. Wren finally speaks plainly: the house keeps whoever finishes the song, and Mei has been holding the last verse in her throat for thirty years. Emotional beat: hope and horror fused—an escape hatch shaped like a trap.

chapters.title: Neighbors
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, daytime. He interviews the elderly neighbor, Mrs. Okafor, who remembers the drowning differently than his mother told it: Mei went into the creek looking for Theo. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: The Creek Bed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He visits the dried creek behind the house and finds the rusted wagon he and Mei played with, plus small bones arranged in the song's rhythm. Wren stands at the tree line, not approaching. Emotional beat: grief made physical, evidence he can't unsee.

chapters.title: Mother's Tape
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Among his mother's boxed belongings delivered by Mrs. Okafor: a cassette labeled 'for when you're ready.' His mother's voice confesses she saw Mei go into the water and said nothing, choosing Theo's innocence over Mei's memory. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Thirteen Doors
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, night. All thirteen doors stand open; behind each, a different year of his childhood replays, all ending at the creek. The frost has reached the interior walls now, writing faster. Emotional beat: being cornered by your own history.

chapters.title: Wren's Hunger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Wren admits what it is: not a friend but the house's appetite wearing a beloved face, grown fat on families who finish songs. It needs Theo's verse most of all—he's the one who stopped singing. Emotional beat: betrayal of the one comfort he had.

chapters.title: Mei's Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A fourteenth door appears, opening onto Mei's preserved bedroom. Her diary details the night: she followed Theo and Wren to the creek, slipped on the bank reaching for him, and the last verse came to her as she went under. Emotional beat: devastating intimacy with the dead.

chapters.title: The Chorus
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He hears them now—every name in the frost, singing fragments in the walls, harmonizing on verses one and two. Among them, faintly, Mei, holding a note no child should hold for thirty years. Emotional beat: horror transfigured into heartbreak.

chapters.title: Learning the Verse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mei's diary contains the words but not the melody; the melody lives in Wren's humming. Theo must let the thing that betrayed him teach him the ending. Sessions at the piano in the parlor, Wren humming, Theo memorizing without opening his mouth. Emotional beat: wary collaboration, trust rebuilt on necessity.

chapters.title: Mother Comes
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His mother arrives at dawn, having read her own tape's echo in her dreams, intending to finish the song herself as penance. Theo physically bars her from the porch as frost takes the yard. Emotional beat: protecting the parent who failed to protect—a reversal, forgiveness in action.

chapters.title: The Last Night
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The house pulls its doors shut one by one, sealing them in. Wren offers a bargain: sing together, be together forever, friends again. The frost reaches the ceiling, spelling THEO. Emotional beat: temptation at its most tender—loneliness weaponized.

chapters.title: Verse Three
chapters.summary: Climax, Theo's POV. In the sealed parlor, Theo speaks Mei's words aloud over Wren's melody—singing the tune alone, never joining voice with the house. The chorus falters; the frost cracks. Wren screams in a voice made of every stolen singer. Emotional beat: triumph through refusal, grief given language.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Falling action, Theo's POV. Dawn. The doors open onto ordinary rooms; the frost melts into plain water. On the porch, Wren flickers—not angry, just smaller—and mouths thank you before dissolving. Theo's appraisal form reads zero. Emotional beat: release, and the strange mourning of losing even a false friend.

chapters.title: What He Told Them
chapters.summary: Resolution, Theo's POV. He tells his mother the whole truth on her porch; she weeps and finally says Mei's name aloud, finishing her own verse. He reports the house structurally unsound, unsellable, and drives away without looking back. Emotional beat: justice outside any courtroom—truth spoken where it was withheld.

chapters.title: Coda: New Houses
chapters.summary: Epilogue, close third on Theo months later. He surveys a cheerful suburban home, counts the doors—ten, correct—and pauses at a child's chalk drawing on the driveway: a stick figure waving. He waves back, just in case, and goes inside to work. Emotional beat: scarred vigilance, tenderness surviving horror.
